narrative_synthesis: Today's meta: (1) short macro reactions (CPI, the Fed) printing 30–47k for Cardone, (2) the 'banks said no' story, which leads straight into seller finance, and (3) the real estate vs S&P fork that TheREDevGUY just started. Drafts: a Philly take on the CPI headline, a 'bank said no' seller-finance story, and a 20-year rowhome vs index fork.

drafts.draft_en:
CPI came in a tenth of a point hot and the market panicked.

In Philly, the seller with a leaking roof and three months of missed payments didn't check CPI today.

Headlines move rates. Problems move deals.

My rule stays the same: purchase plus repairs at or under 65% of after-repair value.

What number are you watching this week?
drafts.pattern: Same-day macro reaction (Cardone '.1 CPI' at 47.1k), brought down to a local distressed seller. Uses Bar's 65% all-in rule; ends on a reply question. No promised returns.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head, 15s. Open with a phone showing 'CPI +0.1' on screen, cut to a Philly rowhome porch, say 'Headlines move rates. Problems move deals.' Put '65% of ARV' on screen.

drafts.draft_en:
The bank told her no.

Good credit, steady job, self-employed. Didn't fit the box.

The seller owned the house free and clear and was tired of being a landlord.

So they skipped the bank: down payment to the seller, monthly payments to the seller, terms on paper.

Sometimes the best buyer is the one the bank sent away.

Would you ever sell with seller financing?
drafts.pattern: 'Banks said no' story → twist → lesson, the format behind wealthmoose's 6.0k post with 41 bookmarks, applied to seller finance. Framed as an example scenario, not a specific real deal. Education, not advice.
drafts.video_tip: Story-time, 25s. Hold a rejection letter prop for the first line, swap it for a handshake shot at 'they skipped the bank', end looking at the camera with the question.

drafts.draft_en:
20 years. $50k to invest.

A) Index fund. Hands off.
B) A Philly rowhome with a loan. Tenants, repairs, and leverage.

Count taxes, cash flow, and your time.

Which one builds more legacy, and why?
